source_text: Liber Quartus. Surge, veni, proxima mea, speciosa mea, columba mea, quoniam ecce hiems transiit, pluvia abiit et discessit sibi; flores visi sunt in terra, tempus putationis advenit, vox turturis audita est in terra nostra; ficus produxit germina sua, vites florentes dederunt odorem. Ordo dramatis supra descriptus; nunc quid sermo Dei ad animam vel Christus ad ecclesiam dicat advertamus.
pass_a_gloss: Book Fourth. Rise, come, near-one my, fair my, dove my, because behold winter has-passed, rain has-gone and departed to-itself; flowers seen are in land, time of-pruning has-come, voice of-turtledove heard is in land our; fig has-brought-forth shoots its, vines flowering have-given odor. Order of-drama above described; now what word of-God to soul or Christ to church may-say let-us-attend.
pass_b_english: The Fourth Book. [[Arise, come, my near one, my fair one, my dove, for behold, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone; the flowers are seen in the land, the time of pruning has come, the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land; the fig tree has put forth its shoots, the flowering vines have given fragrance >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:10-13]]. The order of the drama we described above; now let us attend to what God’s Word says to the soul, or Christ to the church.
notes: Editorial Liber Quartus after Liber III CLOSEOUT.
